title: IP Licensing and Contracts
subtitle: Draft, negotiate and close the agreements that make IP worth money: trademark licences, technology and software licences, assignments, and the clauses that decide every dispute.
summary: Seven modules built around real licences, with a negotiation simulation played from both sides. You leave with a clause bank you have drafted yourself.
outcomes: Write a due diligence memo on an IP portfolio that tells the client what they are actually buying
Draft a grant clause that gives away exactly what was agreed and nothing more
Draft a trademark licence with quality-control provisions that will hold up in India
Separate a software licence from a SaaS subscription and draft the IP clauses for each
Structure and draft a royalty schedule, with audit rights that get used
Draft a copyright assignment that satisfies Section 19 and an employee IP clause that covers the gap the statute leaves
Negotiate the ten clauses that are always negotiated, from either side of the table
about: Licensing is where IP meets money, and where most of the drafting errors that end in litigation are made. This course is for the lawyer who has to turn a term sheet into a signed agreement and the founder who has to read what comes back.

You will work with six real agreements: a food franchise, a pharma technology transfer, a SaaS contract, a brand licence for a celebrity venture, a software assignment and a cross-border patent licence. Each exercise asks you to draft or redraft a clause before you see ours.

The course ends with a two-sided negotiation simulation. You draft the licensor's position, then the licensee's markup, then the compromise. Most students report that this module alone changed how they read contracts.

modules.title: Trademark licences

includes: Six real agreements, anonymised and annotated
Clause bank: grant, quality control, royalty, audit, termination, assignment
Negotiation simulation with positions for both sides
Monthly live drafting clinic, replays included
whoFor: Transactional lawyers who have been handed their first licence
In-house counsel at brand, pharma and technology companies
Founders negotiating with distributors, franchisees or investors
IP prosecution lawyers moving into transactional work
notFor: You want contract law theory rather than drafting
You only need an NDA; there are free ones
You need US or EU-governed templates; this is Indian law throughout

faq.a: Yes. Every template is a Word document you can adapt. They are starting points, not substitutes for judgement.

faq.q: Is there a module on open source?
faq.a: Open-source audits are covered inside the software module. A dedicated open-source compliance course is planned for 2027.
